newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke denies he threatened to quit over EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke denies he threatened to quit over EMU.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke denied on Thursday that he had threatened to resign if the government hardened Britain's stance over the European Union's planned single currency.
"I did not threaten to resign and I am not threatening to resign," a brief Treasury statement issued on Clarke's behalf said.

The statement was issued following a detailed account on BBC radio of events leading up to Prime Minister John Major's reaffirmation on Tuesday that he would not alter his wait-and-see stance on economic and monetary union (EMU) ahead of an election, due by May.

The BBC report spoke of speculation that Clarke, the cabinet's leading pro-European, had threatened to quit if Major bowed to pressure from "Euro-sceptic" Conservatives and ruled out signing up for EMU when it is launched in 1999.
"I do not regard the BBC's account of this week's events as accurate," Clarke said.
